fullPassage: It is natural for people to observe happenings and then seek explanations for why those happenings occurred. But sometimes the reasoning is wrong because of one or more misconceptions. One of these is the ecological fallacy, where an argument claims that there is a causal relationship between two things merely because they occur together. For example, in the 1950s it was found that crime rates were the highest in neighborhoods where immigrants were most numerous. Some people used this "co-occurrence" to argue that immigrants were a cause of crime. But a careful analysis of this situation revealed that immigrants were forced to live in neighborhoods where crime rates were already high; they could not afford more expensive housing in safer neighborhoods. Immigrants themselves committed very few of the crimes. Unless you analyze the claim carefully, you would misinterpret the relationship and thereby construct a faulty belief. For a species born in a time when resources were limited and dangers were great, our natural tendency to share and cooperate is complicated when resources are plenty and outside dangers are few. When we have less, we tend to be more open to sharing what we have. Certain nomadic tribes don't have much, yet they are happy to share because it is in their interest to do so. If you happen upon them in your travels, they will open up their homes and give you their food and hospitality. It's not just because they are nice people; it's because their survival depends on sharing, for they know that they may be the travelers in need of food and shelter another day. Ironically, the more we have, the bigger our fences, the more sophisticated our security to keep people away and the less we want to share. Our desire for more, combined with our decreased physical interaction with the "common folk," starts to create a disconnection or blindness to reality. Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them. Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push — essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains. An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries. The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future. While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.

questions.passage: It is natural for people to observe happenings and then seek explanations for why those happenings occurred. But sometimes the reasoning is wrong because of one or more (A)[misconceptions / confirmations]. One of these is the ecological fallacy, where an argument claims that there is a (B)[random / causal] relationship between two things merely because they occur together. For example, in the 1950s it was found that crime rates were the highest in neighborhoods where immigrants were most numerous. Some people used this "co-occurrence" to argue that immigrants were a cause of crime. But a careful analysis of this situation revealed that immigrants were forced to live in neighborhoods where crime rates were already high; they could not afford more expensive housing in safer neighborhoods. Immigrants themselves committed very few of the crimes. Unless you analyze the claim carefully, you would (C)[misinterpret / clarify] the relationship and thereby construct a faulty belief.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① confirmations — causal — misinterpret: (A) confirmations(확인)은 misconceptions(오해)와 반대로 부적절
✅ ② misconceptions — causal — misinterpret: 원문 일치. 오해(misconceptions) 때문에 추론이 틀리고, 인과관계(causal)를 주장하며, 관계를 잘못 해석(misinterpret)한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ misconceptions — random — misinterpret: (B) random(무작위)은 causal(인과적인)과 의미가 달라 부적절
❌ ④ misconceptions — causal — clarify: (C) clarify(명확히 하다)는 misinterpret(잘못 해석하다)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: misconceptions(오해) → causal relationship(인과관계) 잘못 주장 → misinterpret(잘못 해석)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 신중한 분석이 이민자들이 범죄율이 높은 지역에 살 수밖에 없었음을 '드러냈다/밝혔다'
det.analysis:
❌ ① confirmed: 확인했다 — 분석이 확인한다는 표현도 가능하나 원문은 revealed
❌ ② denied: 부인했다 — 분석이 부인한다는 의미는 맥락과 맞지 않음

❌ ④ concealed: 숨겼다 — revealed의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: a careful analysis revealed = 신중한 분석이 드러냈다. 주어(analysis)와 목적어(that절)의 의미적 연결이 핵심

❌ ④ (A) 형태 — (B) 방식: (B)는 패션 트렌드이므로 방식이 아닌 유행이 적절

questions.passage: As we lack the resources to compute answers _____(A)_____, we distribute the _____(B)_____ across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers.

questions.stem:
다음 글의 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말의 형태로 가장 적절한 것은?

(A) independent  (B) compute

det.analysis:
❌ ① independent — computing: (A)는 동사 compute를 수식하는 부사 필요, (B)는 관사 the 뒤 명사 필요
✅ ② independently — computation: (A) independently는 부사로 compute를 수식, (B) computation은 명사로 the+distribute의 목적어 ←정답
❌ ③ independence — computation: (A) independence는 명사로 부사 자리에 부적절
❌ ④ independently — computing: (B) computing은 the 뒤에 올 수는 있으나 원문은 computation
det.tip: compute answers independently(부사) / distribute the computation(명사)

questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push — essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could <u>dedicate</u> our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 dedicate의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① waste: 낭비하다 — dedicate와 반대 뉘앙스
❌ ② neglect: 무시하다 — dedicate와 정반대
❌ ③ restrict: 제한하다 — 전념한다는 의미와 다름
✅ ④ devote: 바치다/전념하다 — dedicate와 가장 가까운 동의어 ←정답
det.tip: dedicate ≈ devote — 둘 다 '~에 전념하다/바치다'라는 의미. dedicate our brains to = 두뇌를 ~에 전념시키다

questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an (A)[extensive / limited] network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to (B)[restrict / accommodate] more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an (C)[essential / unnecessary] component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① extensive — accommodate — essential: 원문 일치. 광범위한(extensive) 네트워크, 자전거를 수용하고(accommodate), 필수적인(essential) 구성 요소라는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② limited — accommodate — essential: (A) limited(제한된)는 extensive(광범위한)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ extensive — restrict — essential: (B) restrict(제한하다)는 accommodate(수용하다)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ④ extensive — accommodate — unnecessary: (C) unnecessary(불필요한)는 essential(필수적인)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: extensive network(광범위한 네트워크) + accommodate(수용하다) + essential component(필수 구성 요소)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 배달 트럭이 하이브리드보다 훨씬 '효율적인(efficient)' 운송 수단이므로 wasteful은 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① convert — 원문 일치. 자동차 차선을 자전거용으로 전환한다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② animus — 원문 일치. 배달 차량이 적대감의 대상이라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ③ wasteful — 원문은 efficient(효율적인). 배달 트럭이 하이브리드차보다 훨씬 효율적이라는 맥락에서 wasteful(낭비적인)은 반대 의미로 부적절 ←정답
❌ ④ smaller — 원문 일치. 더 작은 가게를 집 가까이 운영한다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: a far more efficient transporter = 훨씬 더 효율적인 운송 수단. wasteful(낭비적인)은 efficient의 반의어

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 배달 차량은 자주 '적대감'의 대상이 되지만 실제로는 필수적이라는 역접 맥락
det.analysis:
❌ ① admiration: 감탄/찬양 — but actually essential이라는 역접과 맞지 않음. 이미 긍정이면 역접이 불필요
✅ ② animus: 적대감 — 원문 일치. 배달 차량이 적대감의 대상이지만(but) 실제로 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 필수 요소라는 역접에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ curiosity: 호기심 — but 역접에 의미적 연결이 약함
❌ ④ indifference: 무관심 — 무관심이면 target(대상)이 되기 어려움

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a strong feeling of being connected to and wanting to keep something you own"

det.korean: 소유물에 대한 연결감과 지키고 싶은 강한 감정 = 집착/애착(attachment)
det.analysis:
✅ ① attachment: 애착 — 소유물에 대한 연결감과 지키려는 강한 감정 ←정답
❌ ② detachment: 초연함 — attachment의 반의어
❌ ③ impression: 인상 — 소유물에 대한 감정이 아닌 외부에서 받는 느낌
❌ ④ assumption: 가정 — 감정이 아닌 추측의 의미
det.tip: attachment = 애착. 본문에서 insecurity stems from their attachment to their possessions로 등장

questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of <u>clarity</u>. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 clarity의 의미와 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① transparency: 투명함 — clarity와 유의어
❌ ② simplicity: 단순함 — clarity와 유사한 의미
❌ ③ purity: 순수함 — clarity와 유사한 방향
✅ ④ confusion: 혼란 — clarity(명확함)의 정확한 반의어 ←정답
det.tip: clarity(명확함) ↔ confusion(혼란). 쓸모없는 물건을 버린 뒤의 명확함의 기쁨이라는 맥락

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"feeling confused and not knowing where you are or what is happening"

det.korean: 혼란스럽고 자신이 어디 있는지, 무슨 일이 일어나는지 모르는 상태 = 방향감각을 잃은(disoriented)

❌ ③ distressed: 괴로워하는 — 정서적 고통이지 방향감각 상실이 아님
❌ ④ delighted: 기뻐하는 — 혼란과 정반대
det.tip: disoriented = 방향감각을 잃은. 본문에서 may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted로 등장

questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 literal의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: literal: (A) 문자 그대로의/사실적인 (추상적 사고 어려움) / (B) 글자 그대로의 (어원적 의미)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 비유적인 — (B) 글자 그대로의: (A) literal은 비유적(figurative)이 아닌 사실적/글자 그대로의 의미
❌ ② (A) 사실적인 — (B) 상징적인: (B) literal은 상징적(symbolic)이 아닌 글자 그대로의 의미
❌ ③ (A) 상상의 — (B) 글자 그대로의: (A) literal은 상상의(imaginary)가 아님
✅ ④ (A) 사실적인/있는 그대로의 — (B) 글자 그대로의: (A) 아이들의 이해가 사실적이라 추상적 상상이 어렵고, (B) 단어의 글자 그대로의 의미 ←정답
det.tip: literal (1) 사실적인/있는 그대로의: 추상적 사고가 어려운 단계 (2) 글자 그대로의: 단어의 어원적 의미
